Updated assessment incorporating the April 2022 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS):
- Domestic banks reported easing standards for C&I loans to large and middle-market firms and for multifamily CRE, with standards largely unchanged for construction, land development, and nonfarm nonresidential CRE. Loan demand from businesses increased for inventory and accounts receivable financing and for plant and equipment investment. 
- On the household side, banks eased standards for credit card loans, saw stronger demand for HELOCs and auto loans, but reported weaker demand for residential real estate mortgages. 
- Foreign banks tightened standards for C&I loans.
These SLOOS results indicate credit supply was still broadly supportive and business loan demand was firm, partially offsetting the negative impulses from elevated inflation, geopolitical risks, China lockdowns, and imminent Fed policy tightening noted in the FOMC statement and Financial Stability Report. Netting these, the stance remains slightly negative but less so than previously assessed.
